summary.text: Josh Gottheimer is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2016 after a career as a Clinton White House speechwriter and in the private sector, at the Federal Communications Commission, and at Microsoft. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, is Vice-Chair of the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, and co-chairs the SALT Caucus. He sought the Democratic nomination for governor in 2025.

paragraphs.text: Gottheimer was born in Livingston, in Essex County, New Jersey, in 1975 and graduated from West Essex Senior High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Pennsylvania in 1997 and a law degree from Harvard Law School in 2004; between them he studied at Pembroke College, Oxford, on a Thouron Award.
From 1998 to 2001 he was a speechwriter for President Bill Clinton, including on two State of the Union addresses, and in 2004 he worked on the presidential campaigns of Wesley Clark and John Kerry.
Gottheimer then worked in corporate communications at Ford Motor Company and at the public relations firm Burson-Marsteller before joining the Federal Communications Commission in 2010.
He served as senior counselor to the chairman of the FCC and later as a general manager for corporate strategy at Microsoft before running for Congress.
He won the 5th District seat in November 2016, defeating seven-term Republican incumbent Scott Garrett, 51.1% to 46.7%, and was re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.
Gottheimer was first sworn in on January 3, 2017; his district includes parts of Bergen, Passaic and Sussex counties.
He serves on the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where he is ranking member of the National Security Agency and Cyber Subcommittee, and on the Financial Services Committee.

He helped launch the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus in 2017 and served as co-chair during the 115th through 118th Congresses; he is now its Vice-Chair, and he co-chairs the SALT Caucus and the Law Enforcement Caucus.
He announced a run for governor of New Jersey in November 2024 and placed fourth in the June 10, 2025 Democratic primary with 11.8% of the vote.
